name: Helix BioSeal Mk.VII Hemorrhage Arrest System
product_name: Helix BioSeal Mk.VII Hemorrhage Arrest System
description:
The BioSeal Mk.VII is an injectable hemostatic foam system delivered via a pressurized 12mL cartridge injector. Upon injection into a traumatic wound cavity, the compound — a proprietary blend of synthetic fibrin analogs, chitosan-derived biopolymers, and platelet-activating peptides — expands to 40x its liquid volume within 4 seconds, conforming to irregular wound geometries and generating immediate mechanical tamponade. The foam cross-links with endogenous clotting factors to form a semi-permanent plug rated for wounds up to 8cm diameter and arterial pressures up to 180mmHg. The Mk.VII iteration introduced a thermal-reactive dissolve trigger: medical personnel can apply a specific low-frequency ultrasound wand (sold separately as the BioSeal Dissolve Probe DS-3) to liquefy the plug cleanly within 90 seconds, preventing the surgical complications that plagued earlier permanent-foam competitors.

What distinguishes the Mk.VII from its predecessors is the integrated chromatic indicator system — the foam shifts from white to deep amber as it saturates, giving field medics a visual bleed-rate assessment without imaging equipment. A secondary chemical marker reacts to infection-indicating bacterial enzymes, turning the foam red as an early sepsis warning. This dual-indicator system was developed in partnership with Cinderblock AI's diagnostic pattern libraries and is now considered standard in Meridian 88 emergency medicine training.

The BioSeal Mk.VII is standard issue for Meridian 88 Tier 2+ citizens' emergency kits, corporate security teams, and licensed paramedical contractors. In the Underbelly and lower-tier zones, counterfeit 'BioSeal' cartridges — often containing inferior foam with no dissolve capability — are rampant on the gray market. These knockoffs, called 'Hardplugs' by street medics, have caused numerous surgical fatalities when hospital teams couldn't remove the plug without extensive tissue damage.
enables: field trauma stabilization without surgical suite
social_impact: The Mk.VII has effectively created a two-tiered trauma survival landscape in Meridian 88. In Tier 2+ districts, survivable hemorrhagic injuries now have near-90% field survival rates, reducing emergency hospital load and enabling corporate employers to tout 'injury-to-recovery' metrics as hiring incentives. In lower-tier zones, the prevalence of counterfeit BioSeal cartridges means that workers and residents who believe they are protected are often worse off than those who use no hemostatic agent at all — Hardplug removal surgeries have become a grim revenue stream for black-market surgical clinics.
story_hooks: A street medic discovers that a batch of counterfeit BioSeal cartridges flooding the Underbelly market contains a tracking compound — someone is using the knockoffs to monitor wound patterns and identify gang conflict locations in real time
A corporate whistleblower claims Helix Biosystems knowingly certified the Mk.VII dissolve probe at a frequency that also disrupts certain neural implant models — a fact buried in the safety dossier

A Tier 1 security contractor is found dead with a BioSeal plug that dissolved prematurely — the dissolve trigger was activated remotely, and someone with access to medical frequencies wanted the wound to reopen
